candidate.mistake_reason: At Step 7, WebSurfer produced an incomplete list of Daniel Craig movies under 150 minutes, omitting major titles like Casino Royale (144 min), Skyfall (143 min), Quantum of Solace (106 min), Defiance (137 min), Logan Lucky (118 min), etc. This data-collection/filtration error set an incorrect candidate pool for subsequent availability checks and ranking.
candidate.first_mistake: Before Step 7, the conversation only contained planning. Step 7 is the first substantive step where the dataset that drives the final answer was established, and it excluded key candidates that could change which movie is the highest-rated available on Netflix US.
candidate.mistake_not_corrected: Subsequent steps never revisited or corrected the incomplete list; they repeatedly checked availability only for the limited set and then concluded at Step 25 that Road to Perdition was the highest-rated option. The missing higher-rated under-150-minute titles were never evaluated for Netflix availability, so the initial omission persisted uncorrected.

confidences.reason: Sound. This constitutes a data-gathering/filtration error. It is the first actionable mistake leading to the wrong outcome, since subsequent availability checks and the final ranking were based on this incomplete pool. The omission was not corrected later; despite a later search mentioning Knives Out, it was never integrated into the candidate set or final comparison. Thus, criteria (1)-(3) are satisfied.

Since later steps only check Netflix availability for titles from this Step 7 list, the omission directly constrains the candidate set and can change which title emerges as highest-rated on Netflix US. No later step revisits or corrects the dataset, so the mistake persists to the final answer. This satisfies all three criteria (mistake, first related mistake, not corrected).

This contradicts the claim that they only checked the limited set from Step 7 and never evaluated omitted titles.
